encounters.cc: Progressive changes in mood, thinking, and movement with cognitive decline necessitating early retirement

lines: Progressive changes in mood, thinking, and movement with cognitive decline necessitating early retirement
The patient, with established histories of hypertension, mixed hyperlipidemia, and psoriatic arthritis previously managed in internal medicine and rheumatology, presents for neurologic evaluation.
Per his wife, over the past several years she has noticed that he has become more forgetful, often misplacing items or repeating the same questions.
Recently, he has struggled to keep track of bills and could no longer manage his work as a financial consultant, leading to his early retirement.
She also reports that he has become irritable and at times displays inappropriate laughter or anger.
In addition, he has developed frequent, unpredictable jerking movements of his face, arms, and legs that worsen with stress and interfere with daily activities.
The patient takes medication for mild hypertension but no psychiatric drugs.
His father reportedly had similar symptoms in his 50s, though no formal diagnosis was made.
He does not use alcohol, tobacco, or illicit drugs.
The patient denies headaches, vision changes, or episodes of loss of consciousness.
On physical exam, he is oriented to person but not to time or place.
His speech is fluent but tangential, and he has difficulty recalling words and following complex instructions.
Neurologic exam shows irregular, nonrhythmic, involuntary movements involving the upper and lower extremities as well as facial grimacing.
Reflexes and strength are otherwise intact.
On mental status testing, he is unable to recall any of three objects after five minutes and struggles to interpret common proverbs.
Gait is wide-based and irregular due to sudden, unpredictable jerks.
MRI of the brain is obtained.
